issues.failure_explanation: To bound the reach $r_t$, Proposition C.1 bounds $\sup_{z \in \mathcal{R}_t} \|\nabla^3 \log p_t(z)\|$ by the supremum over the center-dominated regions $\cup_{i=1}^n \mathcal{B}_t^{(i)}(\theta_t)$, claiming $\overline{\cup_i \mathcal{B}_t^{(i)}} \to \mathbb{R}^d$. However, the log-density ridge $\mathcal{R}_t$ connects distinct data modes and passes directly through intermediate regions where no single mode dominates (e.g., on the bisector $x_1 = 0$ in the two-point example, where $\text{Softmax}_1 = \text{Softmax}_2 = 1/2 < 1 - \theta_t$). In these intermediate regions along the ridge, $\|\nabla^3 \log p_t\|$ is of order $\Theta(h_t^{-3})$ rather than $\mathcal{O}(\theta_t h_t^{-3})$. Consequently, the reach $r_t$ does not scale as $\Omega(h_t^2 \theta_t^{-1}) \to \infty$ as claimed, but is at most $\mathcal{O}(h_t^2)$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must correctly estimate the reach of $\mathcal{R}_t$ across the intermediate inter-mode regions and adjust all dependent tube neighborhood radii accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed positive reach lower bound $r_t = \Omega(h_t^2 \theta_t^{-1})$ blowing up as $t \to 0$ is invalid, and the tube neighborhoods $\mathcal{T}_t(\rho_t)$ cannot have radius $\rho_t = \Theta(r_t) \to \infty$.
issues.title: Reversed reach scaling from restricting third derivatives to single-mode regions
issues.why_classification: The error changes the geometry of the reference manifold and invalidates the claimed reach and tube neighborhood scaling underlying the paper's three-stage inference framework.

issues.failure_explanation: In the proof of Theorem D.1 (Stage 1), the paper observes that $\rho_\delta^2/h_\delta \le d + 2\sqrt{d\zeta\log(1/h_\delta)} + 2\zeta\log(1/h_\delta)$ and infers $\mathbb{P}(\|z\|^2 \le \rho_\delta^2/h_\delta) \ge \mathbb{P}(\|z\|^2 \le d + 2\sqrt{\dots}) \ge 1 - h_\delta^\zeta$. This reverses the monotonicity of cumulative distribution functions: if $A \le B$, then $\mathbb{P}(\|z\|^2 \le A) \le \mathbb{P}(\|z\|^2 \le B)$, not $\ge$. Since $\rho_\delta \le r_\delta = \mathcal{O}(h_\delta^2)$, the ratio $\rho_\delta^2 / h_\delta \to 0$ as $\delta \to 0$, so $\mathbb{P}(\|z\|^2 \le \rho_\delta^2/h_\delta) \to 0$ rather than tending to 1.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must establish that the diffusion trajectories enter a valid neighborhood of positive reach with probability approaching 1 without inverting the Gaussian probability bound.
issues.overall_effect: Stage 1 fails: the inference process $\tilde{Y}_t$ is not guaranteed to enter the tube neighborhood $\mathcal{T}_{T-t}(\rho_{T-t})$ with high probability. Consequently, the conditioning on $\tilde{t}_{\mathrm{in}} \le T-\delta$ in Stages 2 and 3 becomes vacuous.
issues.title: Reversed probability inequality in Stage 1 tube entry guarantee
issues.why_classification: The entry probability theorem fails fundamentally due to an inverted inequality, undermining the validity of the stopping time $\tilde{t}_{\mathrm{in}}$ on which all subsequent dynamical stages are conditioned.

issues.failure_explanation: Theorem 3.3 derives a differential inequality for the tangent residual $\tilde{u}_t^{(i)}$ under the hypothesis that $\tilde{Y}_t \in \mathcal{B}_{T-t}^{(i)}(\theta_{T-t})$ (the dominant basin of mode $i$). To deduce the bound at $T-\delta$, the proof applies Gronwall's inequality integrated across the entire interval $[\tilde{t}_{\mathrm{in}}, T-\delta]$. However, trajectories do not belong to $\mathcal{B}_{T-t}^{(i)}(\theta_{T-t})$ over all $t \in [\tilde{t}_{\mathrm{in}}, T-\delta]$, and trajectories generating inter-mode samples along the ridge never enter any center-dominant region $\mathcal{B}_{T-t}^{(i)}$. Therefore, the differential inequality cannot be integrated over $[\tilde{t}_{\mathrm{in}}, T-\delta]$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must analyze tangent motion along the ridge without assuming confinement to a single mode's dominant neighborhood throughout the sliding phase.
issues.overall_effect: The tangent sliding contraction estimate at $T-\delta$ is unsupported. Downstream results in Theorems 4.1 and 4.2 that rely on the tangent error bound of Theorem 3.3 become unreliable.
issues.title: Invalid Gronwall integration under conditional mode-dominant assumption in Stage 3
issues.why_classification: The core guarantee characterizing tangent sliding toward modes assumes an invariant that is violated along trajectories, invalidating the resulting rate and downstream bounds.
